review_comments:
I'd suggest adding a test confirming that when there are multiple listeners and listener A changes TraceState then listener B should be able to observe that change in the ActivityCreationOptions.TraceState property. The tests above prove that the changes flow from listener->Activity, but I don't think they prove changes flow to other listeners.
(I'm pretty sure the test will pass, just trying to be thorough and make the tests document intended behavior)
That is a good idea. I have added this test case.
More of a design question... if I was a developer using an earlier version of the C# compiler, would I have any way to achieve the same result?

No, to use this feature must use C# compiler version 10 or later. This is not the first feature we expose in the framework using this new syntax. [System.Text.Json](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ae259bff32bd7fb5eee4d5a86a42214c39aba362/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Metadata/JsonObjectInfoValuesOfT.cs#L20) already using it a lot.
I assume @reyang and @cijothomas are OK with this requirement? Effectively they will have to compile OpenTelemetry SDK with a compiler version >= 10.

Just to make sure we are on the same page:

We've discussed about this C# 10 language feature and the understanding is: if we are compiling against an old version of runtime which doesn't provide full support for all C# 10 features, we would get compile time error if such C# 10 feature is not going to work on the target runtime.

In other words, if we don't get compile time error, then we have confidence that such feature would work fine (not having runtime error) on the platforms we targeted.
Regarding why I would call this out - there are some concerns/questions which are beyond my knowledge https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/discussions/2790#discussion-3800306.
That is right. Just ensure you are building for all targeting (ns2.0 and netfx)

> Regarding why I would call this out - there are some concerns/questions which are beyond my knowledge https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/discussions/2790#discussion-3800306.

I replied there too. I will be happy to help with any questions raised there too.
